name: Big Lizard
summary: Sell an ATM straddle and buy one OTM call; a jade lizard with the short strikes pulled to the money, collecting a very large credit with no upside risk when that credit exceeds the call spread width.

legs.strike_rule: SAME ATM strike as the short put
ATM strike + Wc, where Wc satisfies total credit > Wc x 100; typically Wc = 1.5-3.0% of spot

typical_dte: 21-45 DTE; often deployed the session before earnings on a high-IV name
when_to_use: IV rank > 70, typically as a pre-earnings IV-crush trade on a name you are willing to own at the ATM strike. The big credit from the ATM straddle makes the credit > Wc condition easy to satisfy, which is the whole point.
max_profit: net credit received, only at the ATM strike
max_loss: (ATM strike x 100) - net credit on a move to zero. No upside loss when credit > Wc x 100.
breakevens: downside breakeven = ATM strike - credit/100; no upside breakeven when the credit condition holds

greeks.delta: slightly positive at entry (short ATM straddle is near delta-neutral, the long call adds a few deltas)

entry_rules: MANDATORY: net credit x 100 > Wc x 100 (credit in points must exceed the call spread width in points); reject otherwise.
Both short legs on the identical ATM strike (delta 0.45-0.55 / -0.45 to -0.55).
Short put fully cash-secured: reserve (ATM strike x 100) - credit before submission. Level 3 requires this; an uncollateralized ATM short put is Level 4.
Underlying price <= $120 so a single unit's cash-secured put stays under 25% of a $50k account.
Position size: maximum 1 big lizard open account-wide at any time.
All three strikes: OI >= 500, per-leg spread <= max($0.05, 10% of mid).
Single 3-leg limit order at mid, accept mid - $0.05 only if the credit > Wc condition survives.
management_rules: Profit target: close at 25% of the credit received (an ATM short straddle rarely gives back 50% without a big directional move).
Pre-earnings version: close the morning after the report, at the open, regardless of P/L.
Stop: close if the short put delta reaches -0.65, i.e. the underlying has fallen roughly one expected-move unit.
Rolling: if tested down, roll the ATM short put down and out for a credit once; never roll the call spread down.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: an ATM short put and an ATM short call both exist - one of them is ITM at expiry with near-certainty. Flatten every leg by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short put immediately if ITM with extrinsic < $0.10.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close the call spread before the ex-date if the short ATM call is ITM with extrinsic below the dividend - an ATM short call before a dividend is a near-certain early assignment.
PIN GUARD: at 15:30 ET on expiry day, close if |spot - ATM strike| < 0.5% of spot.
Close any ITM short leg by 2 DTE unconditionally.
assignment_risk: Very high. Because the shorts are ATM, one of them is ITM at expiry essentially always. The short put delivers 100 long shares at the ATM strike; the short call delivers -100 shares covered only by the far OTM long call. In a $50k paper account, a single assignment on a $100 underlying consumes $10,000 of buying power instantly. Automated flatten is mandatory.
buying_power: Cash-secured put (ATM strike x 100 - credit) plus (Wc x 100 - call-side credit). The largest BP consumer in this family relative to credit collected.
liquidity_needs: Moderate-to-high; the ATM strikes are the most liquid in any chain, the long call must still show OI >= 500.
common_mistakes: Running it on a $400+ underlying and locking up the whole account in the cash-secured put; taking the trade with credit <= Wc, which quietly reintroduces upside risk; holding through the ATM pin at expiry; treating it as neutral when it is really a short-gamma bomb.
zero_dte_notes: Not recommended. An ATM short straddle at 0DTE combines maximum gamma with near-certain ITM assignment on one side. The system should refuse this slug for 0DTE expiries.
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
bias_note: neutral with a bullish tilt, aggressively short-vol
